headline: President Clinton set up an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between Metro-North Commuter Railroad and some of its unions.
what_it_does: This order creates a temporary emergency board to investigate a dispute between Metro-North Commuter Railroad and workers represented by certain labor unions. Under federal railway labor law, such boards usually study the dispute and make recommendations. While a board does its work, strikes and lockouts are generally put on hold for a set period. The title does not give details about the dispute itself.

who_it_affects.group: Metro-North Commuter Railroad employees in the involved unions
who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute is sent to a federal board for investigation, which typically delays any strike while the board works.
The railroad must take part in the board's investigation and generally cannot lock out workers during the waiting period.
The process typically delays a possible strike that could disrupt their train service.
